def load() -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd
    from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

    path = 'data/legal/input/metropolitan_statistics.html'
    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
        html = f.read()

    soup = BeautifulSoup(html, 'html.parser')

    # Extract all tables; keep raw as strings for robustness.
    tables = pd.read_html(html, flavor='bs4')
    out = []
    for i, t in enumerate(tables):
        t2 = t.copy()
        t2.columns = [str(c) for c in t2.columns]
        t2.insert(0, 'tableIndex', i)
        out.append(t2)

    if not out:
        return pd.DataFrame({'tableIndex': [], 'note': []})
    return pd.concat(out, ignore_index=True)

def process(itTheftRaw) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd
    import re

    df = itTheftRaw.copy()

    # Identify header rows per file and keep only plausible data rows.
    # Data rows typically have a metro name in col0 and a numeric count in col1.
    c0 = 'Metropolitan Areas: Identity Theft Reports'
    c1 = 'Unnamed: 1'

    # Drop obvious non-data rows
    df = df[~df[c0].fillna('').str.contains(r'^Source:', case=False, regex=True)]
    df = df[~df[c0].fillna('').str.match(r'^Metropolitan Area\s*$', case=False)]
    df = df[~df[c0].isna()]

    # Keep rows with numeric report counts
    def to_num(x):
        if x is None:
            return None
        s = str(x).strip()
        if s == '' or s.lower() in {'nan', 'none'}:
            return None
        s = s.replace(',', '')
        m = re.fullmatch(r'-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?', s)
        if not m:
            return None
        return float(s)

    df['reports'] = df[c1].map(to_num)
    df = df[df['reports'].notna()]

    # Keep only rows that look like MSA entries (have a state abbreviation after comma)
    df['metroRaw'] = df[c0].astype(str).str.strip()

    return df[['sourceFile', 'metroRaw', 'reports']].reset_index(drop=True)

def process(itTheft2023, metroPop2023) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd
    import re
    import unicodedata

    def normalize_metro_name(s: str) -> str:
        if s is None:
            return ''
        s = str(s)
        s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', s)
        # Remove common suffixes
        s = re.sub(r'\b(Metropolitan Statistical Area|Metropolitan Area|MSA)\b', '', s, flags=re.I)
        s = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s).strip()

        # Keep only "city and state" portion: usually up to first comma plus state abbr
        # For names like "New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ-PA" keep the whole pre-comma + state string.
        # We'll standardize punctuation/hyphens.
        s = s.replace('–', '-').replace('—', '-')
        s = re.sub(r'[\(\)\[\]\.]+', '', s)
        s = s.replace('&', 'and')
        s = s.lower()
        s = re.sub(r'\s*,\s*', ', ', s)
        s = re.sub(r'\s*-\s*', '-', s)
        s = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s).strip()
        return s

    it = itTheft2023.copy()
    pop = metroPop2023.copy()

    it['metroKey'] = it['metroRaw'].map(normalize_metro_name)
    pop['metroKey'] = pop['metroRawHtml'].map(normalize_metro_name)

    # Drop empty keys
    it = it[it['metroKey'] != '']
    pop = pop[pop['metroKey'] != '']

    # Deduplicate population keys (keep max pop2023 if duplicates)
    pop = pop.sort_values('pop2023', ascending=False).drop_duplicates('metroKey', keep='first')

    merged = it.merge(pop[['metroKey', 'pop2023']], on='metroKey', how='inner')

    # Filter metros > 1M in estimated 2023 population
    merged = merged[merged['pop2023'] > 1_000_000]

    # Average identity theft reports across all matched metros
    avg_reports = merged['reports'].mean()

    return pd.DataFrame([{
        'avgIdentityTheftReports': float(avg_reports) if pd.notna(avg_reports) else None,
        'matchedMetroCount': int(merged['metroKey'].nunique()),
        'matchedRows': int(len(merged))
    }])
input.summary: Normalize and robustly match metro names between identity-theft reports (itTheft2023.metroRaw) and metro populations (metroPop2023.metroRawHtml): normalize Unicode, drop suffixes (Metropolitan Statistical Area/Metropolitan Area/MSA), standardize hyphens/punctuation/case/spacing, and keep city+state portion; inner-join on normalized metroKey; drop unmatched identity-theft entries; filter to estimated 2023 population > 1,000,000; compute mean(reports) across matched rows; output avgIdentityTheftReports plus matched metro/row counts for validation

      def process(itTheftRaw) -> pd.DataFrame:
          import pandas as pd
          import re
      
          df = itTheftRaw.copy()
      
          # Identify header rows per file and keep only plausible data rows.
          # Data rows typically have a metro name in col0 and a numeric count in col1.
          c0 = 'Metropolitan Areas: Identity Theft Reports'
          c1 = 'Unnamed: 1'
      
          # Drop obvious non-data rows
          df = df[~df[c0].fillna('').str.contains(r'^Source:', case=False, regex=True)]
          df = df[~df[c0].fillna('').str.match(r'^Metropolitan Area\s*$', case=False)]
          df = df[~df[c0].isna()]
      
          # Keep rows with numeric report counts
          def to_num(x):
              if x is None:
                  return None
              s = str(x).strip()
              if s == '' or s.lower() in {'nan', 'none'}:
                  return None
              s = s.replace(',', '')
              m = re.fullmatch(r'-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?', s)
              if not m:
                  return None
              return float(s)
      
          df['reports'] = df[c1].map(to_num)
          df = df[df['reports'].notna()]
      
          # Keep only rows that look like MSA entries (have a state abbreviation after comma)
          df['metroRaw'] = df[c0].astype(str).str.strip()
      
          return df[['sourceFile', 'metroRaw', 'reports']].reset_index(drop=True)

          import pandas as pd

          sub = df.loc[df['Metropolitan statistical area'].notna(), ['Metropolitan statistical area', '2024 estimate', '2020 census']].copy()

          for c in ['pop2020', 'pop2024']:
              sub[c] = pd.to_numeric(sub[c], errors='coerce')
      
          sub = sub.dropna(subset=['pop2020', 'pop2024', 'metroRawHtml'])
      
          # Linear interpolation for 2023 between 2020 and 2024 (3/4 of the way)
          sub['pop2023'] = sub['pop2020'] + (sub['pop2024'] - sub['pop2020']) * (3.0/4.0)
      
          return sub.reset_index(drop=True)

      def process(itTheft2023, metroPop2023) -> pd.DataFrame:
          import pandas as pd
          import re
          import unicodedata
      
          def normalize_metro_name(s: str) -> str:
              if s is None:
                  return ''
              s = str(s)
              s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', s)
              # Remove common suffixes
              s = re.sub(r'\b(Metropolitan Statistical Area|Metropolitan Area|MSA)\b', '', s, flags=re.I)
              s = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s).strip()
      
              # Keep only "city and state" portion: usually up to first comma plus state abbr
              # For names like "New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ-PA" keep the whole pre-comma + state string.
              # We'll standardize punctuation/hyphens.
              s = s.replace('–', '-').replace('—', '-')
              s = re.sub(r'[\(\)\[\]\.]+', '', s)
              s = s.replace('&', 'and')
              s = s.lower()
              s = re.sub(r'\s*,\s*', ', ', s)
              s = re.sub(r'\s*-\s*', '-', s)
              s = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s).strip()
              return s
      
          it = itTheft2023.copy()
          pop = metroPop2023.copy()
      
          it['metroKey'] = it['metroRaw'].map(normalize_metro_name)
          pop['metroKey'] = pop['metroRawHtml'].map(normalize_metro_name)
      
          # Drop empty keys
          it = it[it['metroKey'] != '']
          pop = pop[pop['metroKey'] != '']
      
          # Deduplicate population keys (keep max pop2023 if duplicates)
          pop = pop.sort_values('pop2023', ascending=False).drop_duplicates('metroKey', keep='first')
      
          merged = it.merge(pop[['metroKey', 'pop2023']], on='metroKey', how='inner')
      
          # Filter metros > 1M in estimated 2023 population
          merged = merged[merged['pop2023'] > 1_000_000]
      
          # Average identity theft reports across all matched metros
          avg_reports = merged['reports'].mean()
      
          return pd.DataFrame([{
              'avgIdentityTheftReports': float(avg_reports) if pd.notna(avg_reports) else None,
              'matchedMetroCount': int(merged['metroKey'].nunique()),
              'matchedRows': int(len(merged))
          }])
